title: Quantum Information & Bio-Ethics Fellowship Dossier
major: Computer Science & Ethics, Politics and Economics (EPE)

sections.abstract: Maya Lin-Vance is a senior at Yale College pursuing a double major in Computer Science and Ethics, Politics and Economics (EPE), graduating summa cum laude with a 3.96 cumulative GPA. Her capstone research develops provably fair algorithmic allocation protocols for humanitarian resources.
sections.scientific_methodology: Combines game-theoretic mechanism design with formal Z3 SMT solver guarantees. Evaluated on real-world municipal healthcare datasets showing Pareto-optimal distribution while maintaining strict privacy bounds.
sections.impact_and_dissemination: Co-director of the Yale Undergrad Community Robotics outreach program, teaching Python and algorithmic fairness to 120 New Haven high school students. Paper accepted at ACM FAccT 2026.
sections.work_packages: Term 1: Algorithmic fairness formal proof. Term 2: Empirical testing on New Haven civic datasets. Term 3: Open-source toolkit release under MIT license.
sections.budget: Full scholarship grant covers remaining tuition ($64,700) and housing/food ($13,800). Parent share ($4,800) and standard student employment self-help ($3,700) are fully accounted for.

video_transcript: Hello members of the Yale Fellowship Committee. My name is Maya Lin-Vance. My capstone work bridges formal computational verification with real-world ethical resource allocation. With Yale's support, this fellowship will allow me to complete our algorithmic fairness toolkit and deploy it with community partners in New Haven.
